m1-implement-and-demonstrate.title: Replace both `test -f` checks with a portable, argv-passed file-existence check; demonstrate both directions with real exit codes
m1-implement-and-demonstrate.imperative: In tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py ONLY: add a small helper (near write_gated_spine, module scope) that builds a command-kind postcondition string driving a genuine file-existence test through `sys.executable -c '...'` (the house pattern) instead of the POSIX `test` builtin. Pass the target path as a `python -c` argv element (sys.argv[1]) rather than interpolating it into the python source text, and shlex.quote() both the python source and the path when assembling the outer shell command line -- this survives Windows paths (backslashes, possible spaces in a TEMP dir) because shlex.quote wraps anything containing a backslash in single quotes, which a POSIX shell (bash on Windows, sh on POSIX) treats as fully literal with zero escape processing, unlike the naive unquoted f-string interpolation this replaces (unquoted backslash-letter sequences are stripped by the shell, mangling the path). The check must genuinely exit 0 when the file exists and non-zero when it does not -- do not weaken it into an always-pass check, since g3's optional_report.txt postcondition depends on it failing while the file is absent (that failure is what makes the later `waive` test meaningful). Replace both call sites (current lines 67 and 92) to use the new helper. Demonstrate the check both directions YOURSELF before trusting the test suite: run the built command string once with the target file absent (expect non-zero exit) and once after creating it (expect exit 0), and paste both real exit codes into your why. Then run tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py and confirm all tests pass, including the four previously-Windows-only-red tests.
